question: Ticket 42b9ca9594e8 says "test_deposit.py folds a per-run id marked as testing into every row it writes to the live cairn tables, and removes that run's nodes, embeddings and links in a finally block", but outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2 reads "How the TESTING database works. (1) The db proxy is the seam (4.3.1.5.1.4.1.1, 11.3.7): proofs, devices and tools never choose a database; the proxy chooses by session context. (2) The test runner sets the context, never the proof: bin/cairn test and the hollow run open every db session with context=testing, so a proof can neither forget it nor pick live (Law 4). (3) In testing context, writes go only to the TESTING database: same schema, rows from a reserved address range, so a testing address never collides with a live one. (4) In testing context, reads are an overlay: testing rows first, live underneath, live pinned at the seq the run started at. A proof reads live with no fixtures, what it wrote shadows live for that run only, and the run repeats within itself. (5) In live context the proxy never consults the TESTING database, so testing artifacts are invisible to all but the run that made them, by construction rather than by filtering. (6) Each run's testing rows carry its run id and are dropped at run end; the sleep cycle sweeps orphans. (7) A proof over live data asserts invariants, never snapshots; a tooth that needs an exact value writes its fixture into the overlay first. Until the per-box proxy exists, the same routing sits in the store door (db_domain) and moves into the proxy when it is built. WHY: a context the proof sets is a context a proof can forget; the runner is the one place every proof passes through. - akiendelllinux_orchestrator -amm" (The outline states in clause (2) 'The test runner sets the context, never the proof' and in clause (6) 'Each run's testing rows...are dropped at run end; the sleep cycle sweeps orphans.' The ticket's intention describes the proof—not the runner—setting testing markers and the proof—not the sleep cycle—performing cleanup, which directly contradicts these outline principles. (Note: decision D1 correctly rejects this approach and aligns with the outline by riding e4fd instead, but the stated intention remains inconsistent with outline 4.3.1.5.1.5.2.)). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
